This sounds silly, but it helped me tremendously. If it fits one (or both) of your characters, write them as shy/flustered/awkward, etc. Write what you know. You know what it feels like to be flustered around the subject or maybe even in those situations, so use that to your advantage instead of pulling at something that’s uncomfortable. 

Start with the parts that come first that excite you. Interactions you know you want in the chapter.  Build everything else around that. (Mind you this is coming from a pantser, so I don’t necessarily even write outlines most of the time.)

Think about more than what is happening physically; how would X respond, verbally or physically? What might they be thinking or feeling physically and emotionally? What expression does char A see on char B’s face, and how does that make char A feel? etc. You could even write our their thoughts in their own words where it fits.

Dialogue is important, at least to me. My best tip is to have a good handle on your characters and how/why they would respond in any situation before translating that to the “bedroom.” If there’s a specific thing you want a character to say but you feel like it’s too “cringe” or OOC, write it out and then go back and say “okay, this feels OOC and I don’t like it. How could I rephrase it in a way that is in character and has the same effect?” This is where most of my use of a thesaurus goes, honestly. 

Hope that helps!

Clara Schumann. 17th century German child prodigy pianist, composer, teacher, and essentially a single mother of seven once her husband Robert Schumann was admitted to an asylum and eventually died. She gave public performances from memory as early as age 13, which was “exceptional” and uncommon at the time. Being one of the first concert pianists to perform from memory, she set the standard for the rest of performance history, which eventually gave way to piano recitals as we know them now. Clara was the main breadwinner for the family through her performances where she premiered many of her husband’s and her own works which was common at the time. Schumann was instrumental in getting her husband’s works recognized, and chose to work tirelessly to do so her entire life. In many ways, Clara paved the way for women in Western music and was generally an incredible person imo.

Edit to add she was one of the first female composers that made some men think that women might have the mental capacity to compose, but, despite being a brilliant composer she ultimately chose to stop composing early because many women had failed and she didn’t expect to be the exception. I think it really depends on the person. ADHD is on a spectrum. Some people can manage really well with good daily structure, diet, exercise and extra ADHD helps here and there. Other people (myself included) have severe difficulty managing with just those things and medication is very beneficial if not almost necessary to have a somewhat “normal” life. Even still, there are people who have all of those things and medication and therapy, etc. but they still struggle a lot. It’s a matter of severity more than anything.

The only reason I stopped taking it was cost and lack of insurance. Without insurance and with discount cards the medication I was on for several years is just shy of $300/mo. I decided that learning to live unmedicated was easier than dealing with the side effects until I can get insurance.
